questions.text: Who is named alongside Paul and Silvanus in the opening salutation of the epistle?

options.text: Apollos
Timotheus
Barnabas
Tychicus

questions.text: Why does Paul glory in the Thessalonians in the churches of God?

options.text: For their great earthly riches, which they generously gave for the poor
For building a new synagogue where the whole multitude gathered together
For their patience and faith in all their persecutions and tribulations
For driving out the heathen whom they violently chased from their cities

questions.text: What is it a righteous thing with God to recompense to them that trouble the believers?

options.text: He will remain silent and leave the wicked without any recompense or judgment
He will forgive all their sins without repentance and overlook all their deeds
He will grant them earthly wealth that they might turn unto him and be saved
He will recompense tribulation to them that trouble his faithful servants

questions.text: How shall the Lord Jesus be revealed from heaven according to 2 Thessalonians 1:7-8?

options.text: In flaming fire with his mighty angels
In secret silence without visible signs
As an unknown wanderer passing through
In spirit only without any revelation

questions.text: What does Paul always pray concerning the Thessalonians in 2 Thessalonians 1:11?

options.text: That they might abound in earthly wealth and increase their temporal possessions
That God would count them worthy of this calling, and fulfil the work of faith
That they might escape from their persecutors and live in peace in another city
That they might gain worldly dominion and rule over the heathen with authority

questions.text: What must come before the day of Christ, according to 2 Thessalonians 2:3?

options.text: A universal turning of all kings of the earth unto the knowledge of the gospel
A complete worldly peace among all kingdoms and the permanent ending of all war
A falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition
The rebuilding of the city of Jerusalem and the return of all nations thither

questions.text: Where will the adversary sit, shewing himself that he is God (2 Thessalonians 2:4)?

options.text: Upon the throne of Caesar
Upon the mount of Sinai
In the halls of judgment
In the temple of God

questions.text: How shall the Lord destroy that Wicked one (2 Thessalonians 2:8)?

options.text: With the spirit of his mouth, and with the brightness of his coming
With legions of angels who cast him down with sharp temporal weapons
With an earthly tribunal that endureth through many passing generations
With a mighty earthquake that swalloweth up his seat and dominion

questions.text: Why shall God send strong delusion unto them that perish (2 Thessalonians 2:10-11)?

options.text: Because they knew not the written law and never heard the words of preaching from the prophets
Because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved from destruction
Because they gave no silver unto the treasury and refused to distribute of their earthly goods
Because they were strangers of foreign nations and knew not the covenants of the holy people

questions.text: What does Paul exhort the brethren to do in 2 Thessalonians 2:15?

options.text: Flee straightway into a strange country and dwell there in quietness
Cease from all labour and wait in idleness for the coming of the Lord
Stand fast, and hold the traditions which ye have been taught of us
Build a strong fortress about the assembly and watch it night and day

questions.text: What does Paul ask the brethren to pray for in 2 Thessalonians 3:1?

options.text: For great riches of gold to sustain their journey unto Rome and provide food
For swift vengeance upon all adversaries and judgment against persecutors
For deliverance from all manual labour that they might rest continually
That the word of the Lord may have free course, and be glorified with them

questions.text: What does Paul command concerning any brother that walketh disorderly (2 Thessalonians 3:6)?

options.text: Withdraw yourselves from every brother that walketh disorderly
Cast him into prison until he confess his faults and repent
Give him a double portion of alms that he may be comforted
Deliver him unto the magistrates that they may judge him

questions.text: What did Paul command concerning any that would not work (2 Thessalonians 3:10)?

options.text: If any will not pray, neither shall he assemble
If any would not work, neither should he eat
If any will not fast, neither shall he minister
If any will not give, neither shall he receive

questions.text: How should they treat any man who obeyeth not the word of the epistle (2 Thessalonians 3:14-15)?

options.text: Count him as an utter enemy and completely cast him off from all fellowship in the congregation
Deliver him unto the secular magistrates that they may scourge him for his outward misdeeds
Have no company with him, yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother
Expel him forever from the assembly that he may never return into their common dwelling

questions.text: What was the token in every epistle written by Paul (2 Thessalonians 3:17)?

options.text: A seal of red wax impressed at the end of the roll
The mark of a lamb drawn as an apostolic signature
The written confirmation of the elders of Rome city
The salutation of Paul written with his own hand
